description: Found by specled_-dn4.10 cold verification (2026-07-25): lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex valid_decision_affect?/4 accepts any ADR affect prefixed 'repo.' without resolving it against anything, and the 'repo.' namespace is documented nowhere in the .spec/ corpus. Pre-existing; same species of spec↔enforcement drift dn4.10 was carved to fix (reference_validation carve-out). Fix: either document the repo.* namespace and its resolution semantics in decision_governance.spec.md, or remove the prefix exemption if it is dead. Out of dn4 epic scope.

ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: small
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
All of it. Doc-the-namespace branch (removal is ruled out by the evidence above). Four edits:

1. .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:42-48 — amend the `statement:` of requirement `specled.decisions.reference_validation` (stability: evolving) to state the second exception: ADR `affects:` ids in the reserved `repo.` prefix namespace are repo-scoped governance identifiers that intentionally resolve against nothing in the index and are accepted without resolution; define what the namespace means (repo-level policy areas, not spec subjects/requirements/ADR ids) and that it is a literal `String.starts_with?/2` prefix test, not a registry lookup.

2. New file .spec/decisions/specled.decision.repo_namespace_affect_carveout.md (name is a suggestion) — required because edit 1 adds an exception to a `must` requirement and AppendOnly demands a weakening-set ADR whose `affects:` names the requirement. Frontmatter must be: `id:`, `status: accepted`, `date:`, `affects:\n  - specled.decisions.reference_validation`, `change_type: adds-exception`, `reverses_what: >-` (non-empty after String.trim/1 — enforced by CrossField R2 and specled.decisions.cross_field_reverses_what). Body needs the three required sections Context / Decision / Consequences (SpecLedEx.DecisionParser.required_sections()). Model it byte-for-byte on the existing .spec/decisions/specled.decision.deprecates_affect_reference_carveout.md. The Decision section must explicitly supersede the "All other ADR `affects:` links still must resolve" sentence in that frozen ADR and list it under `## Related`.

3. .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:27-32 — add the new ADR id to the `decisions:` list in the `spec-meta` block (the deprecates carve-out ADR is already listed at :32 as the precedent).

4. test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs — add a test tagged `@tag spec: "specled.decisions.reference_validation"` that calls `Verifier.verify/3` with one decision whose `affects` is `["repo.governance"]`, no `change_type`, and no matching subject/claim id, and asserts no `decision_unknown_affect` finding is produced for it (the mirror of the existing "deprecating decisions may affect ids absent from the current index" test at verifier_test.exs:419).

Decide-and-record (do not leave silent): CrossField R4 at lib/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field.ex:145-172 has no repo.* branch and therefore disagrees with the verifier. Either (a) add `String.starts_with?(affect, "repo.")` filtering to `first_unresolved/2`'s input for R4 and amend `specled.decisions.cross_field_affects_resolve` (.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:101-110) with the same exception, or (b) state in the new ADR's Consequences that CrossField is deliberately stricter and is unreachable in the live gate today. Option (a) is strongly preferred because specled_-4a6 is chartered to wire CrossField into the live path.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md, .spec/decisions/specled.decision.repo_namespace_affect_carveout.md, test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs, lib/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field.ex

== RISK NOTES ==
ORDERING — HARD DEPENDENCY WITH specled_-4a6. 4a6 ("Wire CrossField.validate/3 into the live decision-parse path") would make lib/specled_ex/index.ex:31 pass a current_index into DecisionParser, which activates CrossField R4 (cross_field.ex:145-172). R4 has no repo.* exemption, so the instant 4a6 lands, all five committed ADRs carrying `- repo.governance` emit `cross_field/affects_unresolved` and `mix spec.check` on this repo's own corpus goes red. 14t MUST land before or together with 4a6, and 14t's CrossField decision (option (a) above) must be taken, not deferred. Both tickets edit the same regions: cross_field.ex `apply_rule(:r4_affects_resolve, ...)` and the `cross_field_affects_resolve` / `reference_validation` requirements in .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md. Assign both to one implementer or serialize them.

REALIZATION HASHES — the recommended doc-only edits (1,2,3) touch no hashed binding: zero drift. Two ways to accidentally cause drift:
  - Editing lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2095-2101 (the "remove the exemption" branch, which the evidence rules out anyway). `SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4` is bound at the `implementation` tier (.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:25-26) and that tier is TRANSITIVE — lib/specled_ex/realization/implementation.ex:10-21 hashes the tracer-emitted callee closure with shared helpers inlined, so the private `valid_decision_affect?/4` is inside verify_decision/4's hash input. Its baseline is .spec/realization_hashes.json:651-654 ("SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4", hash 6c4100ca…). Any body change there requires a baseline update and will trip `branch_guard_realization_drift`.
  - Editing cross_field.ex is SAFE for hashes: `SpecLedEx.DecisionParser.CrossField.validate/3` is bound at `api_boundary` (.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:23), and api_boundary.ex:228 `defp normalize_clause({args, guards, _body})` discards bodies, so changing the private `apply_rule(:r4_…)` clause does not move that hash. There is no realization_hashes.json entry for it either.

SHARED SPEC FILE — .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md is edited by both 14t and 4a6; requirement ids `specled.decisions.reference_validation` and `specled.decisions.cross_field_affects_resolve` are the contested region. Both are `stability: evolving`, so AppendOnly permits change with a weakening-set ADR; do not let two tickets author two competing ADRs against the same requirement id.

SOFT CONFLICTS — adding a new file under .spec/decisions/ interacts with specled_-4pl (that ticket repairs "four absolute stem-occurrence counts" inside .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md; a new ADR that happens to use those stems shifts the counts 4pl is pinning — land 14t first, then let 4pl recount) and with specled_-ozm (its stale-allow-marker sweep scans @marker_scope ".spec/decisions/", test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:176).

GATE NOTE — test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:227-243 lints every finding-code-shaped token in .spec/**/*.md against real implementation codes, with only a `length(files) > 50` floor (currently far above it), so adding one ADR is safe. But the new ADR prose and the amended requirement statement must not name a finding code that has no implementation counterpart; `decision_unknown_affect` and `cross_field/affects_unresolved` both exist today (verifier.ex:1925, cross_field.ex:163) and are safe to cite.

VERIFICATION — decision_governance's tagged_tests entry (.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:133-145) already covers specled.decisions.reference_validation with execute: true, so the new test in item 4 is credited automatically; no spec-verification block edit is needed.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate (edits 1-4 plus the decide-and-record item),
which is what you implement.

## ORCHESTRATOR DECISION on the CrossField question — do not defer it
The admission offers (a) add `repo.` filtering to CrossField R4 and amend
`specled.decisions.cross_field_affects_resolve`, or (b) record in the ADR that
CrossField is deliberately stricter.

TAKE OPTION (a). Reason: specled_-4a6 is chartered to wire `CrossField.validate/3` into
the live decision-parse path. The moment that lands, R4 activates and every committed
ADR carrying `- repo.governance` emits `cross_field/affects_unresolved`, turning this
repo's own gate red. Option (b) would leave a live landmine for a ticket that already
exists. Option (a) is safe for realization hashes:
`SpecLedEx.DecisionParser.CrossField.validate/3` is bound at `api_boundary`, and
api_boundary discards function bodies, so changing the private `apply_rule(:r4_…)`
clause moves no hash.

NOTE ON 4a6: it was CUT from this epic and remains open standalone, so there is no
in-epic ordering constraint. You are landing the exemption first, which is the correct
order.

## Allowed touches
- `.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md` — the `reference_validation` statement
  (edit 1), the `spec-meta` `decisions:` list (edit 3), and the
  `cross_field_affects_resolve` statement (option a).
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.repo_namespace_affect_carveout.md` — NEW file
  (edit 2). Model it byte-for-byte on the existing
  `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.deprecates_affect_reference_carveout.md`.
- `test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs` — one new test (edit 4).
- `lib/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field.ex` — option (a) only.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex` — the "remove the exemption" branch is ruled out by the
  ticket's own evidence, and editing it WOULD move a realization hash:
  `SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4` is bound at the `implementation` tier, which is
  TRANSITIVE, so the private `valid_decision_affect?/4` is inside its hash input. Do not
  touch it.
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.deprecates_affect_reference_carveout.md` — it is
  frozen. Your new ADR SUPERSEDES its "All other ADR `affects:` links still must resolve"
  sentence by saying so in your own Decision section and listing it under `## Related`.
  Do not edit that file.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (orchestrator consolidates once at the end), `VERSION`,
  `.spec/realization_hashes.json`, `.spec/state.json`.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent)
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json` MUST NOT CHANGE. A diff there means you edited
  `verifier.ex`. Revert and report.
- The new ADR's frontmatter is gate-enforced: `id:`, `status: accepted`, `date:`,
  `affects:` naming `specled.decisions.reference_validation`,
  `change_type: adds-exception`, and `reverses_what:` NON-EMPTY after trim (CrossField R2
  and `specled.decisions.cross_field_reverses_what` both enforce it). Body needs all
  three required sections: Context / Decision / Consequences.
- Edit 1 adds an EXCEPTION to a `must`. That is a weakening, which is exactly why the
  ADR in edit 2 is mandatory — AppendOnly demands a weakening-set ADR whose `affects:`
  names the requirement. Do not do edit 1 without edit 2.
- Define the `repo.` namespace precisely: repo-level policy areas, NOT spec subjects,
  requirements, or ADR ids; and a literal `String.starts_with?/2` prefix test, not a
  registry lookup.
- No new dependencies.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs` plus any CrossField test file you touch
3. `mix format --check-formatted`
4. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`
5. `git diff --stat -- .spec/realization_hashes.json` must be EMPTY.
6. PROVE THE CARVE-OUT BY EXECUTION: show that a decision whose `affects` is
   `["repo.governance"]` produces no `decision_unknown_affect` finding AND no
   `cross_field/affects_unresolved` finding, and paste the output. If you take option
   (a), also show that a NON-`repo.` unresolvable affect STILL produces the finding —
   otherwise you have disabled the check rather than carved out a namespace.

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. The orchestrator owns
whole-system proof at the merge gate and PR CI.

IMPLEMENTED

CrossField R4 now filters `repo.*` ids via literal String.starts_with?/2 before unresolved lookup (option a), matching the live verifier without touching verifier.ex or realization hashes. Tagged verifier test pins acceptance of `affects: ["repo.governance"]` with no change_type and no matching subject/claim.

Epic lessons checked against diff:
- [stale-spec] ADR describes the shipped remedy (prefix exemption + CrossField R4 filter), not a removal path
- [stale-spec] Rule is satisfiable via the same String.starts_with?/2 the verifier already uses

TEST_CRITIC: FAIL

Session: b19669f0-1a1a-42a6-b6f8-39da90177a9c
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/b19669f0-1a1a-42a6-b6f8-39da90177a9c.jsonl

Findings:

BLOCKING

- (d) New production branch in CrossField R4 has zero test coverage.
  `lib/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field.ex:162` now calls
  `reject_repo_namespace(affects)` and `:291` defines it. `grep -c 'repo\.'
  test/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field_test.exs` returns 0 — no
  CrossField test constructs a decision with a `repo.`-prefixed affect.
  Deleting `reject_repo_namespace/1` and restoring the old call would leave
  the entire cross_field_test.exs suite green. Nor is the branch covered
  indirectly: `SpecLedEx.Verifier` never calls CrossField (only
  `lib/specled_ex/decision_parser.ex:67` does), and the verifier has its own
  independent predicate at `lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2095`
  (`valid_decision_affect?/4`). The verifier test added by this ticket
  exercises the verifier predicate only — the two paths share nothing but a
  string literal.
  This matters more than "an untested helper" because the spec change in the
  same commit amended `specled.decisions.cross_field_affects_resolve`
  (`.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:108`) to *state* the `repo.`
  carve-out, and that requirement's `tagged_tests` leg
  (`.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:154`) resolves via the
  cross_field_test.exs `@moduletag spec:` list. The leg is green while
  nothing pins the clause the requirement now claims — a requirement asserting
  behavior no test can falsify.
  Correct version: add to the existing `describe "rule 4: affects must
  resolve in current index"` block (`cross_field_test.exs:176-205`), mirroring
  the shape of the R6 test at `:322-337`:

      test "repo-prefixed affects are accepted without resolving" do
        d =
          decision(%{
            "id" => "adr.a",
            "status" => "accepted",
            "affects" => ["repo.governance"],
            "change_type" => "narrows-scope",
            "reverses_what" => "scope is too broad"
          })

        errors = CrossField.validate(d, index(subjects: ["subj.x"]))
        refute "cross_field/affects_unresolved" in codes_in(errors)
      end

  Note the fixture must use a non-`deprecates` `change_type` (as above), or
  the R6 branch at `cross_field.ex:157` short-circuits first and the test
  passes without ever reaching the new filter — a false green.
  Optionally pair it with a mixed-list case (`["repo.governance",
  "subj.nope"]` → still errors on `"subj.nope"`) to pin that the filter
  narrows rather than disables R4.

NON-BLOCKING

- (c) Minor: the `@tag spec:` at `test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:455` is
  spelled correctly — exact match for `- id:
  specled.decisions.reference_validation` at
  `.spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:43`, and that id is in the
  `tagged_tests` covers list at `:147`. But it is redundant: the module
  already carries that id in its `@moduletag spec:` list
  (`verifier_test.exs:33`). ExUnit test-level tags override module-level tags
  on key collision, so this line does not add a tag — it *replaces* the
  22-entry module list with a single entry for this one test. Harmless here
  (the test still runs under `--only spec:specled.decisions.reference_validation`,
  and it genuinely is not about the other 21 subjects), but the line reads as
  additive and is not. Either drop it or, if the intent is deliberate
  narrowing, that is worth a comment.

WHAT PASSES

- (a) The negative assertion is load-bearing, not decorative.
  `verifier_test.exs:479` is a bare `refute "decision_unknown_affect" in
  finding_codes(report)`, which alone would rot. It is anchored by
  `:481-485`, which asserts a `decision_affect_valid` *pass* check exists with
  the exact message `"Decision affect valid: repo.governance"`. That is a
  positive assertion about the predicate's return value, not about the absence
  of output: `verifier.ex:1723-1745` emits `decision_affect_valid` only on the
  true branch and `decision_affect_invalid` on the false branch, so the assert
  proves `valid_decision_affect?/4` returned true *for that specific affect
  string*. If the fixture degenerated — decision dropped, `affects` list
  emptied, decision never reaching the affect loop — no check with that
  message would be emitted and the test fails. The `debug: true` flag needed
  to populate `report["checks"]` is passed at `:475`.
  Residual weakness, not blocking: if `decision_unknown_affect` were renamed,
  the `refute` goes vacuous. That is caught elsewhere — `:407-415` asserts
  `finding_codes(report) == MapSet.new([...])` by equality, so a rename fails
  there loudly.

- (b) The paired positive exists, in the same file: `verifier_test.exs:351`
  `"verify validates decisions and subject decision references"`. Its second
  decision (`:389-398`) carries `"affects" => ["missing.subject"]` — a
  non-`repo.` unresolvable affect with no `change_type` — and `:407-415`
  asserts `decision_unknown_affect` is in the exact finding-code set, with
  `:417` asserting a `decision_affect_invalid` check. So the suite does
  distinguish "carve-out works" from "resolution check disabled" on the
  verifier path. (It also already exercised the `repo.` branch implicitly at
  `:384` via `["repo.governance", "package.subject"]`; the new test makes that
  explicit and adds the no-`change_type` case.) The equivalent discriminator
  exists on the CrossField side too (`cross_field_test.exs:178-190`) — it is
  only the positive half that is missing there, per the blocking finding.

- (e) Fixture honesty is acceptable. The test hand-builds the index map rather
  than parsing a real ADR, but that map *is* `Verifier.verify/3`'s public
  input contract — every other test in the file uses the same shape via
  `base_subject/1`, and decision parsing is a separate unit with its own
  tests. The hand-built map does not bypass the code under test; it enters at
  the same door `mix spec.check` uses. No end-to-end parse→index→verify test
  for a real `.spec/decisions/*.md` carrying `affects: [repo.governance]`, but
  that matches the coverage posture of the sibling deprecates test at `:419`
  and is not a regression introduced here.

- (f) Clean. No `Process.sleep`, no spawned or unmanaged processes, no shared
  tmp. `root` comes from `SpecLedEx.FixtureCase`
  (`test_support/specled_ex_fixture_case.ex:14-24`), which builds a per-test
  path from `System.system_time(:nanosecond)` +
  `System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])` + 4 random bytes and
  `File.rm_rf`s it `on_exit` — no collision hazard even under the module's
  `async: false`. The new test does not touch `root` at all. The module's
  `async: false` is pre-existing and documented (`verifier_test.exs:2`,
  VM-global `System.put_env` PATH shims); the one `Process.sleep(20)` in the
  file is inside the pre-existing `process_dead?/2` poll loop, out of scope
  and a bounded poll rather than a fixed synchronization sleep.

VERIFICATION RUN

  mix test test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs \
           test/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field_test.exs
  → 82 tests, 0 failures (seed 585121, 50.2s)

  Green — which is exactly the point of the blocking finding: the CrossField
  suite is green with and without the new `repo.` branch.
